title: After five people on the same phone network or Wi-Fi save a Quick advert in a day, every other newcomer on that connection is told 'Too many adverts from this connection today' and cannot save hers until tomorrow.
fix: Stop counting signed-in sessions (move `hits.append` inside `if not sess`), count only successful new-account creations, and raise the per-IP cap substantially (e.g. 50/day) while relying on the existing per-address mail cap (_DRAFT_MAIL_MAX) to stop abuse; keep the log in Redis/DB rather than process memory.
impact: Exactly the people Quick is built to spread to (the person beside her, a township on one mobile NAT, workers at one employer's Wi-Fi) are locked out for 24 hours with no workaround except changing network.

title: An employer-enrolled worker who scans her slip again after making an advert (or a phone-code user after the first hour) lands on TrustSquare looking signed out and cannot reach her advert or her introductions, because the app ignores the valid sign-in the link just gave her.
fix: In open_enrolment, when has_advert, redirect to _mint_signin_url(ident, <latest draft or live id>, 20) exactly as /k/ does (inject the minter via configure); and in ms.js _msInit, when ms_aa_email is absent, call GET /quick/me with credentials and adopt a signed_in email/name (cookie-proven) before routing — which also covers phone-code sessions.
impact: On a new phone/browser, or if she missed the 60-minute button, her 'never-lapsing' key opens a signed-out front page — her draft can't be published and introductions can't be seen.

title: A housekeeper's, nanny's or caregiver's Quick advert shows her area, working days and rate to every stranger the moment it is published, before any employer has vouched for her or a police clearance is verified — the protection David ruled for these women is not in the server.
fix: Add a visibility predicate to get_listings (all branches) and to the non-owner branch of GET /listings/{id}: hide Services/Casuals listings whose seller has no earned 'universal.employer_confirmed' or 'universal.id_verified' credential, and for the police_clearance/licence roles require that signal; Quick should send the role key (svcPickIn(picks,'what').r) so the server knows the role's gate.
impact: An unvetted woman's free days and working suburb are public to anyone, which the ruling calls a safety risk to her (and for child-care roles, to families).

title: The 'your advert is waiting' and 'your advert is live' emails promise the button works for 7 days, but it stops working after 3 days or after the first tap, and then drops her on the sign-in screen even if she is already signed in.
fix: Mint these letters with a 'draft_return' purpose (7-day, reusable, not subject to SIGNIN-ONCE-1) or fix the copy to state the real 72h/one-time rule; in ms.js, on a failed verify check `_msIsSignedIn()` and route to dashboard+msLandDraft() instead of signin.
impact: Re-opening the letter to find her advert (very common) or opening it on day 4-7 fails with an error and loses the draft landing; QUICK-RETURN-TTL-1 / AUDIT-S2 are silently undone.

title: Workers enrolled by an employer, and WhatsApp-link users making another advert, are told 'Introductions reach you by SMS' (or 'We emailed you a link') although no phone or email is on file.
fix: In quick_publish, look up `users.phone` for the key identity and only return identity 'phone' when it is set, else 'link'; word quick.html's .ar-small by r.identity and never claim SMS for a key account with no phone.
impact: She waits for SMS or email that will never come while buyers' introduction requests sit unseen in her hub (and ignored introductions can get adverts blocked under EULA 14.5 B3).

title: Quick can file an advert under the wrong city — and for overseas sellers the wrong country — because it looks the chosen area up in a South-Africa-wide list where the alphabetically first city with that suburb name wins, overriding the city she picked.
fix: In the override, keep window.QCITY when the picked area is in QP.cities[QCITY]; only resolve free-typed areas via `/geo/cities?country=`+QCC; prefer QCITY on a name collision.
impact: Her advert is shown to buyers in another city (a New Yorker's in Cape Town with a $ rate, a Rosebank cleaner in Cape Town), where nobody who can hire her will see it.

title: Quick tells every seller her trust score is 0 or 'trust not opened yet' and ranks her advert on that, while TrustSquare puts her real trust (40 for a newcomer, higher for members) on the advert that buyers see.
fix: Return trust_score from /quick/me for signed-in members (and the canon base 40 for strangers) and set SELLER.ts from it before drawDraft.
impact: The 'three scores' she is taught in Quick disagree with what she and buyers see in the app, undermining the one-scorer promise.

title: Quick adverts drop out of price filters and jump to the top of 'highest price' sorts: new adverts have no numeric price until the next server restart, and a band such as 'R1 000–R5 000' or a rate like 'R350 / call-out + R300 / hour' is then read as R10 005 000 or R350 300.
fix: Parse the FIRST number only (with k/m multiplier) in create_listing/update_listing, in the boot backfill, and in ms.js's priceNum.
impact: A buyer filtering 'under R1 000' never sees the R100–R500 Local Market item, and price sorting puts it among R10 million adverts.

title: Publishing a property advert (one tap in Quick for a member, or the Publish button in the app) can hang for up to about 30 seconds while the server looks up nearby schools and shops on a slow public map service.
fix: Move the POI auto-link out of the request: `background_tasks.add_task(...)` or `threading.Thread(target=auto_link_pois, ..., daemon=True).start()` as already done at bea_main.py:3082.
impact: The one-tap publish looks frozen on a phone, inviting a second tap or abandonment.

title: When SMS codes are switched on, a Kenyan, Namibian or Mozambican seller who types her number the local way gets her code sent to a stranger's South African phone and can never confirm.
fix: Pass the country from Quick (QCC) into /auth/phone/start and normalise using that country's calling code; reject local-format numbers for non-ZA countries.
impact: Outside South Africa the phone key silently fails and texts one-time codes to unrelated people.

title: An employer's enrolment page always says none of her people have published, even when they have live adverts.
fix: Change the query to `listing_status='live'` (or `LOWER(listing_status)='live'`).
impact: Organisations using the new employer door (ORG-ENROL-1) see a false 0% uptake and may chase or re-enrol people who already published.

title: People who use a WhatsApp link or phone code as their key see a meaningless code like 'w-3f9a0c12bd' as their name ('Publishing as w-3f9a0c12bd') and a fake-looking email address in the app.
fix: For key identities return name None from quick_me/_establish_user_session (front-ends then show 'You'/'Your account'), and never display a @key.trustsquare.co address.
impact: Confusing for a first-time user who never chose that name or address and may think she must use it to sign in.

title: If more than eight people on one shared connection type their sign-in code within ten minutes, the next one is refused with 'Too many attempts', even with the right code.
fix: Count only failed codes per IP (mirror `_rate_ok`/`_rate_note_failure`) in a dedicated bucket with a higher ceiling; keep the per-address budget as the brute-force guard.
impact: At a busy moment behind a carrier NAT, correct codes are refused and the person must wait up to ten minutes.

title: Messages shown to sellers in Quick contain double hyphens ('We emailed you a link -- open it to publish') and, when SMS fails, raw provider codes such as '(bulksms 401)'.
fix: Replace ' -- ' with ' — ' in these user-facing strings and drop the provider info from the 503 detail (log it instead).
impact: Looks unfinished and leaks internal provider details to users.

title: The Buzz explainer shows internal rule codes and developer notes to any seller who taps "See how it works".
fix: Remove the ruled / not-ruled badge and the RUL-122 note. Use: "It arrives as a notification on their phone. If notifications are off, it goes to their email. It is free — no SMS." and "This is an example. Nothing is sent from this screen." Replace "(Shown here so you can see it; …)" with "You each switch this on once, in the TrustSquare app."
impact: A seller sees rule numbers, an API path and design-review notes; the product looks unfinished and the notes explain nothing to her.

title: The save step, the "saved" screen and several other screens have no translation entries, so every non-English user gets English exactly where the advert is saved.
fix: Add these strings to roles/quick_i18n.json for all four languages, and use whole-sentence keys instead of fragments (e.g. one key "Free. Before it goes live you read and sign the {terms} in the app."). Afrikaans for the main ones: "Stoor my advertensie", "Stoor tans…", "E-pos", "Foon", "WhatsApp-skakel", "Gratis. Voordat dit sigbaar word, lees en teken jy die TrustSquare-bepalings in die app.", "Teken die bepalings en plaas dit", "Jou privaat sleutelskakel", "Stuur my sleutel vir myself op WhatsApp", "Stuur Quick vir iemand anders", "Ons soek op TrustSquare…", "Niemand het dit nog in {stad} geadverteer nie.", "Volgende — 3 dae oop".
impact: The door promises "Your advert, your language.", but an Afrikaans, isiZulu, isiXhosa or Sepedi user meets English on the one button that saves her advert and on the screen that confirms it.

title: 177 of the 416 translated labels have no isiZulu, isiXhosa or Sepedi text, so those three languages fall back to English on the tap flow of six of the seven categories.
fix: Fill zu, xh and nso for the 177 keys before those languages are offered on those categories; until then, show a one-line notice in the language menu ("Some categories are still in English").
impact: A Sepedi, isiZulu or isiXhosa user who swipes to any category other than Services gets English questions and English buttons right after choosing her language.

title: The draft screen tells a new seller her advert is "ready to publish", but her button only saves a draft and publishing happens later in the app.
fix: When the button says "Save my advert": flag "Your advert — ready to save", ring "You can add it in the app before you publish.". Keep "ready to publish" and "after you publish" only when the button says "Publish".
impact: She reads "ready to publish", taps once, and may believe the advert is live and never open the app to sign the terms.

title: The door promises "no typing", but the price step and the save step both need typing.
fix: "A few taps and your price. Your advert, your language."
impact: The first screen makes a promise that the fourth screen breaks, which costs trust with first-time, low-literacy users.

title: The "saved" screen says the same things twice and shows the server's English sentence with double hyphens.
fix: Do not print the server detail here; send a short code and word it in Quick (translated). Use: card "Your advert is saved."; one line "Next: open it in TrustSquare, sign the terms and publish."; small print "We also emailed you a link." (e-mail) / "Keep this link — it is your key. Send it to yourself on WhatsApp now." (link). On failure: "Too many adverts from this phone today. Please try again tomorrow." and "Something is missing from this advert. Please try again."
impact: On the most important screen she reads "saved" twice and "we emailed you a link" twice, in English whatever language she chose, with "--" instead of a dash.

title: The save box spells email two ways ("E-mail", "No e-mail needed" next to "Your email"), while the TrustSquare app always writes "email".
fix: Use "Email" / "email" everywhere: tab "Email", "No email needed. …".
impact: Two spellings side by side in one small box look careless.

title: Quick calls the thing an "advert", but its score panel says "listing", and the TrustSquare app she is sent to calls it a "listing".
fix: Use one word for what a seller publishes in both apps. Quick already says "advert" to its users, so either change the app's user-facing "listing" to "advert", or at least make Quick consistent: "advert score", "every advert you make", "Car adverts ask for more details than most".
impact: A first-time seller who taps "Finish it in the app" lands on screens about her "listing" and may not connect it to the advert she just made.

title: Quick calls every other person "she" or "her", even when the example contact is a man or a company.
fix: Use "they/their" or "the other person": "Hold your phones close … towards their phone — or let them scan the code with their camera.", "Making the code…", "They will see:", "They get their own Quick …", "Waiting for them to accept…", "Accepted — Quick is on their phone.", "They said no thanks. Nothing was shared.", "They answer the same two questions when they join from your link.", "If their notifications are off, it goes to their email instead."
impact: A man passing Quick to his brother, or a seller whose contact is an agency, reads text that is plainly about someone else.

title: The score panel uses internal abbreviations (RS, TS, LS) and phrases a first-time user cannot decode.
fix: Tiles "Ranking", "Trust", "Advert". "Your ranking is half trust and half advert quality. It goes up when either of them goes up." Heading "Cars — what raises your trust score". "Car adverts ask for more details than most — 5 instead of 1 — so they start lower and can climb higher." "Your trust score starts when someone who knows your work vouches for you, or when you pass an ID check." Put the two no-point items under their own label "Before you publish".
impact: The one place that explains the score uses code names, so it explains nothing to the seller.

title: Two example screens say things were sent or accepted when nothing is sent.
fix: Label both as previews and word them conditionally: header "Example — this is what your employer sees"; "In the app, this sends Marie Fourie and Johan de Wet one buzz each, with your name on it."; "When they continue, they accept the TrustSquare terms."; "+18 trust — what her score would gain."
impact: A seller may type her own email thinking she has signed up, or wait for replies to a phone-around that never happened.

title: "Ask your traders instead" is the wrong word for most categories, and one screen names the same action three ways.
fix: Button "Ask people you know"; line under it "One short message to each of them — up to five."; empty state "Ask people you know, or browse everything on TrustSquare."
impact: Someone looking for a cleaner, a tutor or a flat has no "traders" and will not tap the button.

title: The advert text Quick writes can contain grammar and meaning errors that buyers will read.
fix: "1 bedroom" / "{n} bedrooms"; join the last two items with "and" ("I speak English and isiZulu."); "Best time to go: winter."; prefix role answers ("Ages: babies, toddlers.", "Cares for: an older person, a person with a disability."); use "/ person" for a day trip.
impact: Public adverts go out with "1 bedrooms" and misleading lines under the seller's name.

title: "Flick the icon towards her phone" and "Send to a nearby phone" promise a direct phone-to-phone send, but the app only opens the share menu or copies a link.
fix: "Let them scan the code with their camera — or share the link."; button "Share the link"; hint "Flick up to share".
impact: People will hold two phones together, flick, and think it failed when a share menu appears instead.

title: A returning member's banner says "Publishing as" and "nothing re-asked", even when the button only saves a draft.
fix: "Saving as {name}" ("Publishing as" only when the button says Publish); drop "nothing re-asked"; make "change" read "Change this in TrustSquare" and link to the profile.
impact: "nothing re-asked" is internal shorthand, "Publishing as" is untrue for an unsigned member, and "change" leads nowhere.

title: The "Another option" screen says "The six above are only the ones we see most", but nothing is above it and the list is often not six.
fix: "The list only shows the most common answers. What you type goes on your advert exactly as you type it." Button "Next".
impact: The sentence points at choices that are not on screen, confusing exactly the user who could not find her option.

title: The reference card's heading and wording do not tell the seller what to do.
fix: Heading "Ask for a one-line reference"; text "{Your employer} writes one sentence about you. That opens your trust score — nothing you write about yourself can. It takes them four taps, and they never have to use TrustSquare again."; button "See what they will see".
impact: A seller does not learn that she should ask her employer or a customer for a one-line reference.

title: In isiZulu, isiXhosa and Sepedi the advert says "I work in {place}" for every category, including cars, property and goods for sale.
fix: Use the "I work in" form only for Services, Housekeeping and Tutors; for goods, property and trips use a neutral "{what} — {place}." (or the language's own "in/at {place}"), confirmed by a first-language reader.
impact: A public advert for a car, a flat or a collectable says the seller works in that suburb.

title: An Afrikaans advert still contains English in the price and language lines.
fix: Translate units and names: "Tarief: R300 per dag." (per uur, per besoek, per taak, per uitroep, "+ onderdele"); "Prys: Onder R1 500 per persoon per nag."; "Ek praat Engels en Afrikaans." (English → Engels, SASL → SAGT, and "en" before the last item); "Laagste toegelate bedrag: R241.84 per dag — die nasionale minimumloon."
impact: Buyers read a half-English advert under the seller's name after Quick promised "Your advert, your language."

title: Several Afrikaans compound words are misspelt or split.
fix: "Teëllêer"; "Lugversorgings- en verkoelingstegnikus"; "Swaarnywerheid & masjinerie"; "Dit is onder die nasionale minimumloon." and "Laagste toegelate bedrag: $1 — die nasionale minimumloon."; "Enige NKR-kwalifikasie of kortkursus" (keep "NQF-" if that is the term sellers know; "kortkursus" is one word either way); "onderwyservriend"; "bv. Ken iemand 'n wiskundetutor vir Graad 10?".
impact: A native Afrikaans reader spots these at once on the role list and the rate screen.

title: Some Afrikaans labels use a word with a different meaning.
fix: "Nutsman"; "Masjienoperateur (TLB / graafmasjien)"; "Hoe seldsaam?" with "Skaars" and "Net seldsaam"; "Vervoer & voertuie"; "Selfry"; "Ambagstoets geslaag"; "Ons het ook 'n skakel na jou advertensie vir jou ge-e-pos."; "Eers 'n kwotasie"; "Per taak".
impact: The seller picks the wrong option or reads an odd label, and a collector cannot tell "Scarce" from "Rare only".

title: A handful of Afrikaans sentences have word-order or missing-word errors.
fix: "Meer werd as enigiets anders wat jy nou kan doen."; "Jy kan dit in die app byvoeg nadat jy jou advertensie geplaas het."; "Wat gebeur nadat jy jou advertensie geplaas het"; "Tik op elke dag waarop jy vry is. Tik weer op 'n dag om dit af te haal."; "Konsepvertalings – lesers gaan dit nog na. Tik enige tyd om terug te skakel."; "Tik op een om 'n voorstelling te vra — dit gaan in TrustSquare oop, waar jou voorstellings en Tuppence is."
impact: These are on the draft screen, the days step, the language menu and the find results, where an Afrikaans speaker reads them every time.

title: Quick offers Sepedi, but the TrustSquare app's language menu still offers Sesotho unless its language layer is switched on.
fix: Make the app's default list match the South African ruling: English, isiZulu, isiXhosa, Afrikaans, Sepedi.
impact: A Sepedi reader who moves from Quick to the app finds Sesotho in the menu instead of her own language.

title: Afrikaans reference lines need a comma where the verbs of two clauses meet.
fix: "… vir wie jy klas gee, sê", "… vir wie jy gewerk het, sê", "… wat jy ontvang het, sê", "… wat al by jou gekoop het, sê", "… te doen gehad het, sê", "… gehuur of gekoop het, sê", "niks wat jy oor jouself skryf, kan dit doen nie".
impact: Without the comma the two verbs run together and the sentence reads clumsily.

title: The Afrikaans set uses three verbs for list/publish and two words for trip.
fix: "Plaas dit"; "Adverteer iets anders"; "Wat adverteer jy?"; "Nog nie geadverteer nie"; "Soek 'n reis" / "Adverteer 'n reis"; "Elkeen hiervan tel by jou advertensietelling"; "Soek hulp".
impact: Different words for the same action make the Afrikaans read like several translators' work.

title: A few Afrikaans labels read as literal translations.
fix: "Word raakgesien vir werk — binne 'n minuut"; "… in hierdie hele app"; "Skoolgaande kinders"; "Meer as R2 000" (and the others); "Motorwasser"; "Swembadonderhoud"; "Kyk na my advertensie"; "Vir watter ouderdomme sorg jy?".
impact: They are understandable but sound translated, which a native speaker notices.

title: Dashes are written three ways: "—", " - " and "--".
fix: Use a spaced em dash " — " everywhere (or split into two short sentences).
impact: Mixed dashes look unedited, especially side by side on the same card.

title: Some sentences shout single words in capitals.
fix: "These raise your trust score, not your advert score", "The agency paid.", "One agency at a time.", "Many at once.", "… and it ends the day it sells.", "This link is my key to it".
impact: Capitals read as shouting and break the calm tone of the rest of the app.

title: Apostrophes are sometimes straight (') and sometimes curly (’).
fix: Use the curly ’ in all visible text (straight quotes only inside code).
impact: Minor, but the mix shows on the same screens.

title: The code is called "6-digit" and "six-digit" in the same box.
fix: "6-digit code" everywhere ("A 6-digit code comes by SMS.", "Type the 6 digits from the SMS.").
impact: Small inconsistency on the sign-up step.

title: The days step uses "open", "free?" and "available" for one idea, and asks a person which days she is "open".
fix: Question "Which days can you work?"; cell label "yes" when picked and nothing otherwise; hint "Tap every day you can work. Tap again to remove it."; button "Next — 3 days".
impact: "free?" under a day can be read as "no charge?", and three words for one idea slow a first-time user down.

title: "What do you hold?" does not say it asks about qualifications.
fix: "Which qualification do you have?" (free hint "Type your qualification").
impact: A welder or plumber on a cheap phone may not know what to answer.

title: Some labels on main screens are codes or unexplained terms: bare language codes, "★ is trust", "Tuppence", "push", "SASL".
fix: Door row with names ("English · isiZulu · isiXhosa · Afrikaans · Sepedi"); "★ = trust score"; "Tap one to ask for an introduction — it opens in TrustSquare."; "… and email catches it if their notifications are off."; "Sign language (SASL)".
impact: A first-time user cannot tell that NSO means Sepedi or what "push" and "Tuppence" are.

title: The Services Buzz facts say "A stranger cost a Tuppence" — wrong tense, and the app writes "1 Tuppence".
fix: "A new customer costs 1 Tuppence. Your own regulars are free."
impact: Reads as a typo and uses a different form of the currency from the app.

title: The minimum-rate line always says "/ hour" and "the national minimum wage", even for per-visit or per-job prices and for countries whose floor is another minimum.
fix: Per visit / job / call-out: "Lowest allowed: R30.23 — one hour at the minimum wage."; say "the legal minimum wage" instead of "the national minimum wage".
impact: A seller typing a per-job price is told an hourly figure and may think her job price is being checked as an hourly rate.

title: Some country swaps and examples do not fit other countries: a "bakkie" becomes a "small car" and SA-only wording stays.
fix: GB swap "bakkie" → "pickup"; show a country-specific phone example (or "Type your mobile number"); apply the "matric" swap to the level chips too.
impact: Users in the other eight countries see South African terms or a changed meaning.

title: Three Sepedi role names still contain English words.
fix: Ask the Sepedi reader for native terms (e.g. "Khoutu 10 / 14"); drop or translate "excavator" and "shuttle".
impact: English words sit inside the Sepedi role list.

title: The old publish path still holds developer text; it is switched off today but would show if the newer code failed to load.
fix: Delete the unused joinThen()/doPublish() text, or reword it for users.
impact: One script error in the QUICK-NEXT-1 block would put rule codes and raw JSON in front of sellers.

title: The tester report sheet gives Windows keyboard steps on a phone app and shows raw browser errors.
fix: On touch screens: "Take a screenshot, then tap here to add it."; on failure: "Could not send — nothing was lost. Please try once more."
impact: Phone testers get instructions they cannot follow and an error they cannot read.

title: The US legal cards use US spellings, unlike the rest of the app (this file is loaded by the TrustSquare app, not by Quick).
fix: "Trade Licence", "Outfitter Licence", "need a licence", "licensing", "scrutinise", "programmes" (keep official names such as "Commercial Use Authorization"), or record a decision that US cards use US spelling.
impact: Spelling changes between country cards of the same feature.

title: Rand thousands and "NaTIS" are written differently in Quick and in the app's trip and legal cards.
fix: Write rand with a space for thousands everywhere ("R2 450", "R5 200") and use "NaTIS" in both.
impact: Small inconsistency a careful reader notices when moving between the two apps.

title: The Terms that sellers must scroll through before publishing still contain internal drafting notes and code names.
fix: Delete the notes and code names from the published text: remove the 'must be confirmed by legal counsel', 'Solar Council', 'placeholder' and '[Note: …]' sentences; write the server line as 'stored on the Platform's servers in Germany (EU), hosted by Hetzner'; replace 'AdvertAgent' with 'AI features', 'Anonymity Gate / Mode B' with 'Anonymity Gate', and drop '(Principle A8)'.
impact: A seller reading the binding terms is told the terms are unfinished and unchecked by a lawyer, and meets internal code names; this undermines trust at the exact moment of acceptance.

title: The app tells sellers both that ID verification is optional and that buyers cannot reach them until they verify.
fix: Pick one rule and say it everywhere. If the block stays: success screen 'Buyers can request introductions once your ID is verified with Home Affairs (1 Tuppence) — My Space → Trust.'; Home Affairs card 'Buyers can only request introductions once you are verified.'; and change Terms 3.5A to match. If verification is meant to be optional, remove the blocking button and toast text instead.
impact: Sellers skip verification because they are told it is optional, then never receive a request; the upload-ID advice sends them down a path that does not unblock them.

title: Local Market buttons tell buyers they pay 1T, but the form they open says introductions are free for buyers.
fix: On Local Market screens use one line: 'Request introduction · free for you' (the seller pays 1T). Keep the modal text 'The seller pays 1T when you request — nothing is charged to you.'
impact: Buyers see two different prices for the same tap and may abandon the request or distrust the charge.

title: The free plan says the card is verified at signup, but no card is ever taken and the same screen says no card is required.
fix: Use 'Free forever — no card needed' on every Free plan card and drop 'card verified' everywhere.
impact: Sellers either fear they must hand over a card, or believe a card was checked when it was not; the two lines on one screen contradict each other.

title: Transaction history shows raw ledger codes, job IDs and type keys instead of plain descriptions.
fix: Map every type to a label (e.g. ai_hold 'AI report — held', ai_release 'AI report — released, not charged', intro_hold 'Introduction — held', intro_burn 'Introduction — paid', lm_credit 'Local Market refund') and write descriptions for people: 'AI report: Expedition dossier', 'Top-up via Paystack'. Show 'Balance: 366T'.
impact: People checking what they paid for see developer identifiers they cannot read, on the one screen that should explain their money.

title: Sellers are told banking details are required for Tuppence payouts, but the app has no payouts and no banking form.
fix: Remove the banking card, tip and 'payout details' wording until banking and payouts exist. Sell-flow line becomes: 'Your listing goes live on the free plan straight away. Your account details and plan can wait — we email you a sign-in link.'
impact: Sellers go looking for a settings page that does not exist and expect money that will never be paid.

title: The AI Features screen shows developer wording, a 'testing phase' note and the raw AI model name.
fix: Footer: 'You pay only when your report arrives. If it fails, nothing is charged.' Checkbox: 'Sample preview — free (untick for the full report)'. Status: 'Starting your report…', 'Working on it… (1–4 minutes)', 'Done in 42s — 3T used'. Button: 'Get the report · 3T'. Failure: 'That did not work — nothing was charged.' Remove the model line. Toast: 'Sample mode: your photos are not analysed — untick Sample preview for the full report.'
impact: A paying user meets payment jargon (hold, commit, burn) and is told the feature is in testing, which makes the charge feel unsafe.

title: The Billing tab can tell a real seller they are an 'admin test account' with a 'dev override'.
fix: Remove the dev text. If a raised limit must show: 'Your listing limit: {limit} (set by your agency).'
impact: A real agency agent reads that they are a test account, which looks like a broken or fake account.

title: The agency console shows ticket code names (SEAT-SUB-1, RG-0167) and the jargon 'ops-set' to agency admins.
fix: Badge: 'Pro seat · paid'. Tooltip: 'Set up by TrustSquare after a manual payment.' Replace 'with ops' with 'being checked by TrustSquare', 'ops needs it' with 'we need it', and '(MIRA gate)' with '(MIRA registration required)'.
impact: Agency admins, who are paying business customers, see internal ticket numbers and staff shorthand.

title: Five texts show a raw backslash before the apostrophe, e.g. "I\'ll" and "buyer\'s".
fix: Use a plain apostrophe: "buyer's", "I'll", "don't", "you'll".
impact: Visible code characters look like a broken page in the Terms and on buttons.

title: Two spelling mistakes on buyer screens: 'electricers' and 'Collectors item'.
fix: "Plumbers, electricians, cleaners and more." and "🏺 Collector's item".
impact: Spelling slips on category and listing screens look careless to first-time visitors.

title: Category descriptions promise checks and services TrustSquare does not provide.
fix: Tutors: 'Find tutors for any subject or age. See each tutor's Trust Score before you ask for an introduction.' Collectors: 'Rare finds, vintage items, trading cards and collectibles — see each seller's Trust Score.' Cars: 'Buy or sell vehicles. Every seller shows a Trust Score; contact details stay private until you both agree.' Services: 'Plumbers, electricians, cleaners and more near you.' Local Market: 'Your neighbourhood marketplace — fresh produce, handmade goods and local deals.'
impact: Buyers may assume items and sellers were checked and rely on that promise.

title: The wallet card says Tuppence is earned by completing deals, which never happens, and offers a 'pack' that does not exist.
fix: Subtitle: '1 Tuppence = 1 introduction ($2)'. Button: 'Buy Tuppence'.
impact: Users wait for Tuppence they will never earn and look for packs that are not sold.

title: The 'how your introduction works' steps on every listing have grammar slips and one line that says the opposite of what it means.
fix: "You send an introduction request"; "The seller has 48 hours to accept or decline"; "No reply within 48 hours → seller's Trust Score −5 · you pay nothing"; "Sellers are asked to reply within 48 hours".
impact: Buyers read broken English on the main buying screen, and 'ignored within 48hrs' reads as if the seller ignored it early.

title: Property sellers see 'Why sellers use a estate agent'.
fix: Build the phrase with the right article: 'Why sellers use an estate agent' (and 'a car sales agent', 'a tour agent').
impact: An obvious grammar error on the main Property selling path.

title: The agent banners on Property and Cars read 'Plan it with a Real Estate Agent' and 'Plan it with a Cars Buy/Sell Agent'.
fix: Property: 'Buy or sell with an estate agent'. Cars: 'Buy or sell with a car sales agent'.
impact: 'Real estate' is American, 'Plan it' does not fit buying a house or car, and 'Cars Buy/Sell Agent' is clumsy on a main browse banner.

title: Every listing card and detail uses internal model names ('Commit', 'Queue', 'Commitment Model', 'Soft Queue') that buyers will not understand.
fix: Card badges: '⏳ One buyer at a time' and '👥 Open to several buyers'. Detail headers: '⏳ One buyer at a time — the listing pauses for you' and '👥 Several buyers can ask at once'. Paused badge: '⏸ On hold for a buyer'.
impact: First-time buyers cannot tell what 'Commit' or 'Soft Queue' means for them.

title: The AI helpers go by many names, and two messages name the vendor 'Claude'.
fix: Use 'AI Coach' for listing help and 'our AI' in progress messages ('⏳ Our AI is reading your cards…', '✨ Our AI is rewriting your listing…'); retire 'Listing Coach', 'dashboard coach' and 'photo reader'.
impact: Users cannot tell whether these are one feature or several, and the vendor name will be wrong if the AI provider changes.

title: The app gives three different prices for the AI Coach.
fix: State one rule everywhere, e.g. 'AI Coach: free while you create a listing; after publishing, 1T per session (your first session is free).' Remove '· free' from the explainer steps.
impact: Sellers cannot tell whether coaching costs Tuppence, so they either avoid it or are surprised by a charge.

title: The Seller Hub welcome and the AI Coach explainer describe a different flow from the one the button opens.
fix: Welcome: 'Start with List with AI Coach — pick a category, fill in the details and add photos; the coach suggests improvements.' Explainer last step: 'You publish — buyers can then find it and request an introduction.'
impact: Sellers expect a one-photo shortcut and meet a long form; 'goes live as a pending draft' contradicts itself.

title: The same thing is called a 'listing' in most of the app and an 'advert' elsewhere, and the Quick app mostly says 'advert'.
fix: Use 'listing' in both apps (the Terms' defined word and the Quick Listing app's own name), e.g. 'Publish my listing', 'In a hurry? 5-tap Quick listing ›'; and write 'email', never 'e-mail'.
impact: A seller who creates an 'advert' in Quick then manages 'listings' in the app may think these are different things.

title: The seller's home screen has five names: My Hub, My Seller Hub, Seller Hub, Seller hub and dashboard.
fix: Call it 'Seller Hub' everywhere: header button 'Seller Hub', title 'Seller Hub', 'Go to my Seller Hub →', 'from your Seller Hub'.
impact: Sellers told to go to 'your dashboard' cannot find a screen of that name.

title: The emailed sign-in link has six names, and the sign-in button promises a link while the confirmation talks about a code.
fix: Say 'sign-in link' everywhere (the email carries a link and a code): button 'Email me a sign-in link and code'; confirmation '✓ We emailed you@… a link and a 6-digit code. Tap the link, or type the code below.'; 'Session expired — open your latest sign-in link.'
impact: Users hunting for a 'magic link' or a link when the screen asks for a code get stuck signing in.

title: The Terms go by six names, and one message tells sellers to 'complete your EULA'.
fix: Call it 'Terms of Use' everywhere (menu, footer, checkbox, gate titles); keep 'EULA' only inside the legal text; toast: '… activated — accept the Terms of Use to go live.'
impact: Sellers may think they are accepting several different documents, and 'EULA' is jargon to most people.

title: Error messages show raw HTTP codes, server text and technical words.
fix: Show plain messages and keep codes out: 'Something went wrong on our side — nothing was lost. Please try again.'; 'Could not turn on pings on this phone. Please try again later.'; 'Pings on for this phone.'; 'We couldn't reach the server, so we're showing everything.'
impact: Users cannot act on a status code, and technical words make the app feel broken.

title: Sellers editing a listing are asked to accept the Local Market terms, whatever their category.
fix: Use a separate Terms of Use gate for this case ('Accept the Terms of Use to save your changes' plus a link to the full Terms), and keep the Local Market modal only for Local Market listings.
impact: A Property or Tutors seller is asked to agree to paying per request, a rule that does not apply to them.

title: The Terms contradict the app, and themselves, in several places.
fix: Align the Terms with the app: describe the blurred profile photo in 3.1; describe the real acceptance button in 2.4; drop 'planned but not yet live'; write 'Schedules A–G'; state one server fact; use −5 in 5.3; title 'End User Licence Agreement'.
impact: Sellers accepting the Terms read rules and screens that do not match what they use.

title: The AI Services list tells users where to find tools using paths that no longer exist.
fix: Remove the Batch Cards entry until it is back in the Sell flow; write 'Open one of your listings in Seller Hub → Edit → ✨ Rewrite'.
impact: Users follow the directions and cannot find the tool they are paying for.

title: Every plan says 'All features included', but some features are Pro only.
fix: Free: 'All selling tools included'. Starter: 'Everything in Free, plus 10 listing slots and 2 Tuppence a month'. Pro: 'Everything in Starter, plus the AI research suite and Squire'.
impact: Free and Starter sellers are promised features they will then find locked.

title: Two seller screens always say 'Pretoria', whatever city or country the seller is in.
fix: Fill in the seller's city ('Manage listings & profile · {city}') or drop the city: 'Manage your listings and profile' / 'Sell on TrustSquare'.
impact: Sellers in Cape Town, Nairobi or London are told they are in Pretoria.

title: The language menu's built-in list still offers Sesotho instead of Sepedi.
fix: Make the fallback list English, isiZulu, isiXhosa, Afrikaans, Sepedi (nso); map a saved 'st' to 'nso' (or English) on start; stop the server allowing 'st' for South Africa.
impact: Contrary to the ZA ruling (Sepedi replaced Sesotho), some readers get machine Sesotho under a label that says English.

title: Afrikaans: 'live' is translated as 'regstreeks' (live broadcast) or 'lewend' (alive), while the Quick app says 'aanlyn'.
fix: Use aanlyn/sigbaar: "Gaan aanlyn →", "Jy is aanlyn", "Amper aanlyn", "Jou advertensie is nou aanlyn op TrustSquare.", "Veranderings is dadelik sigbaar.", "… met 'n aktiewe advertensie", "Die advertensie bly sigbaar…". Use one verb for publishing in both apps — 'Plaas' (as Quick does, the idiomatic 'plaas 'n advertensie').
impact: Afrikaans sellers read broadcast or 'alive' wording on the publish path, and the two apps use different words for the same step.

title: Afrikaans: several words mean something else, including the badge on every Property listing card.
fix: "⏳ Verbintenis"; "Handrat"; "Laerskool"; "Alles is welkom — vintage-vondste, tweedehandse en skaars items."; "Die topverkoper"; "✨ 'n Nuwe weergawe is pas vrygestel"; "Het jy 'n beoordelaarkode of adminwagwoord?"; "Een reël, reguit na die foon van iemand saam met wie jy reeds werk — met jou naam daarop." (and "Een reël, reguit na hul foon"); "· per keer", "'n regte uitvoering", "'n mislukte versoek kos niks nie"; "Ons soek passings in elke kategorie, insluitend die Plaaslike Mark."; "Peuters"; "Nutsman"; "(TLB / graafmasjien)"; "👥 Oop tou" (or the new English wording translated).
impact: Afrikaans readers get the wrong meaning on listing cards, filters, plans and the Buzz and AI screens.

title: 'Trust Score' is written three ways, and is sometimes shortened to just 'Trust'.
fix: Always 'Trust Score' (capital T and S), including in Quick; write 'Trust Score −5', never 'Trust −5'.
impact: The product's key signal looks like different things in different places.

title: Prices are formatted three different ways.
fix: South African style everywhere: 'R1 250 000' (no space after R, a space between thousands, no cents unless needed), e.g. 'R6 500 pp / night', 'R20 000', 'R0'.
impact: The same amount looks different from screen to screen.

title: A spaced hyphen is used as a dash in ten places, where the rest of the app uses an em dash.
fix: Use a spaced em dash ' — ' for every dash, e.g. 'You're offline — top-up needs a connection'.
impact: Inconsistent punctuation looks unfinished.

title: Three full stops are used instead of the ellipsis character in a few places.
fix: Use '…' everywhere, e.g. 'Redirecting to secure payment…', 'Search everywhere — e.g. safari weekend, BMW 1996…'.
impact: Minor inconsistency.

title: Apostrophes and quotation marks switch between straight and curly.
fix: Use straight quotes and apostrophes (' and ") everywhere, as most strings already do.
impact: The same word renders differently on neighbouring screens.

title: Buttons and headings mix Title Case and sentence case, sometimes for the same label.
fix: Sentence case for all buttons, headings and labels: 'Publish listing', 'Top up Tuppence', 'Save draft', 'Is this a fair price?', 'Request introduction', 'Confirm top-up', 'Select country'. Keep capitals only for names (TrustSquare, Trust Score, Tuppence, Local Market, Seller Hub, AI Coach).
impact: Looks unpolished; the same button changes style between screens.

title: Hours and the Tuppence unit are written several ways.
fix: Write '48 hours' and '24 hours' in full; write Tuppence amounts as '5T' (no space) and balances as 'Balance: 366T'; write '2 MB'.
impact: Small inconsistencies across the same flow.

title: A few US spellings remain in a British/South African app.
fix: 'analysed', 'speciality', 'towards', 'any time', 'End User Licence Agreement', 'estate agent'.
impact: Minor, but the house style is British/SA English.

title: Small grammar slips in several places.
fix: 'ID received — waiting for confirmation.'; '2, 1 and 1 pt'; '{n} years' experience' / 'Years of experience'; '14 days' in-app notice'; 'a travel agency that does'; 'bulk import'; 'higher-quality buyers'; 'If the seller declines or does not reply… The seller loses Trust Score points for not replying.'; 'Sign in to use the Why no intros? audit'; 'Kid-friendly', 'Beginner-friendly', 'Pet-friendly'; 'your Trust Score and listing summary'; if David agrees, 'AI-GENERATED EXAMPLE ADVERT'.
impact: Each slip is small, but together they make the app read as unedited.

title: 'Introduction' and 'intro' are mixed on the same screens.
fix: Use 'introduction' in sentences, buttons and anything about money; allow 'intro' only in tight chips and badges.
impact: New users may not realise 'intro' is the paid Introduction.

title: Rentals are called 'For Rent' in the buyer filter but 'To Rent' or 'To Let' when sellers list.
fix: Use 'For Sale' and 'To Rent' everywhere (filter, chips and sell flow).
impact: Minor inconsistency between what sellers pick and what buyers filter.

title: The link preview and home feed use off-brand wording: 'mobile-first local marketplace' and 'the Square'.
fix: og:description: 'A global marketplace where you meet trusted sellers through an introduction. Sellers stay anonymous until you both agree.' Feed heading: 'Today on TrustSquare'.
impact: 'Mobile-first' is industry jargon in a preview ordinary people see, and 'the Square' is a nickname used nowhere else.

title: Agent ranking is explained with four names and two unexplained abbreviations.
fix: Use two plain names: 'Trust Score' and 'Listing quality', and one sentence: 'Ranking = half Trust Score, half listing quality.' Drop TS, SPS and Match Rank.
impact: Sellers and agents cannot tell that 'listing quality', 'Agent Score', 'SPS', 'Match Rank' and 'Best Match' describe the same ranking.

title: A fading listing is labelled 'refresh to stay visible', which sounds like reloading the page.
fix: '🌙 Fading — tap Keep live to stay visible' (and show the Keep live button in this state).
impact: Sellers reload the page and the listing still fades.

title: The Tuppence screen says you pay when you 'choose to connect', but you pay when the seller accepts.
fix: 'Each Tuppence pays for one introduction. You pay only if the seller accepts your request.'
impact: Buyers may think tapping Request already costs them.

title: The heritage feature is called 'World Heritage', 'World Wonders' and 'wonders'.
fix: Call it 'Landmarks' (covers UNESCO sites, national parks and museums): 'Nearby landmarks', 'Maximum 5 landmarks per listing', 'Sign in to manage landmarks'.
impact: Sellers may not connect the edit-screen feature with the home section.

title: Other language sets: no keys are missing, but a few common words are left in English.
fix: Translate these when the Sepedi review happens; Afrikaans: 'Casuals' → 'Los werkers', 'Magic Link' → 'Aantekenskakel' (or retire the term in English first).
impact: Minor: a handful of English words inside otherwise translated screens.

title: Afrikaans mixes 'KI' and 'AI' for artificial intelligence.
fix: Use 'AI' in both apps: 'AI-diens', 'AI-afrigteroproep', 'AI ontleed tans jou advertensie…', 'Ons AI sien jou advertensie na…', 'Pro AI-reeks', 'AI-navorsingsreeks', 'AI-voorbeelde'.
impact: The AI Coach appears as both 'AI-afrigter' and 'KI-afrigter'.

title: Afrikaans progress messages read as commands.
fix: Add 'tans': 'Laai tans jou advertensie…', 'Lees tans jou foto's…', 'Skryf tans jou beskrywing…', 'Ontleed tans jou mark…', 'Laai tans erfenisterreine…', 'Laai tans…'; and 'Ons gebruik jou besonderhede om iets oortuigends te skryf'.
impact: Readers may think they are being asked to do something while the app is working.

title: Afrikaans leaves well-known South African park names half in English.
fix: "Tafelberg Nasionale Park", "Weskus Nasionale Park", "Addo-olifant Nasionale Park", "Bergkwagga Nasionale Park", "Blyderivierspoort-natuurreservaat", "Skeletkus Nasionale Park", "Antoninusmuur", "Noord-Masedonië", "Ou Stad van Lamu".
impact: Afrikaans readers know these places by their Afrikaans names; the half-English forms look machine-made.

title: Afrikaans polish: missing double negatives, split compounds, a Dutch form and a few awkward phrases.
fix: "Nooit enige kommissie nie"; "Geen kommissie nie — kopers skakel direk"; "Hoekom geen voorstellings nie?"; "Dienstipe"; "📈 Opbrengsrekenaar"; "Antiek"; "Halfpensioen"; "Heeldag"; "‹ Terug na tuisblad"; "✕ Herstel tuisblad"; "Enige vertrouevlak"; "Hoe vra jy betaling?"; "Soek passende advertensies binne Suid-Afrika."; "Verbeter jou Trust Score met AI-leiding"; "Watter gebied?"; "Kode 10- / Kode 14-bestuurder"; for Featured consider "Uitgelig" (the Afrikaans word; 'Uitgelicht' is the Dutch one).
impact: Each is small; together they make the Afrikaans read as translated rather than written.

title: After saving an advert that is not live yet, the 'Send it to myself on WhatsApp' note links to a page that says 'That listing is not available any more' instead of her advert.
fix: Build the note from the same target as the button: var back=openUrl||('https://trustsquare.co'+(live?'/?listing=':'/?draft=')+id); use back in waMsg (the ?draft= path routes her to sign-in and then to the draft).
impact: The WhatsApp copy, the way back for people who do not read email, opens a dead page and suggests her advert was deleted.

title: Tapping 'List something else' after saving with the WhatsApp-link option creates a second anonymous account, so her second advert sits behind a different key link from her first.
fix: In quick_publish's link branch add response: Response and call _establish_user_session(em, response); on the client, after a link save set QUICK.member=true; QUICK.identity='key' so the next save runs as that session. (Same direction for email saves, whose second advert currently comes back 'You already have a TrustSquare account'.)
impact: A worker who lists two kinds of work gets two accounts, two keys and split introductions and trust; losing either link strands that advert.

title: On many ordinary phones Quick's front screen does not fit: the headline runs over the top bar and logo, and 'Pass Quick on' and the saved-advert card are cut off with no way to scroll to them.
fix: Let the door scroll instead of centring overflow: .screen.door{justify-content:flex-start;overflow-y:auto} .screen.door>:first-child{margin-top:auto} .screen.door>:last-child{margin-bottom:auto} (or justify-content:safe center), raise the short-screen breakpoint to max-height:720px, and hide #logo while #qtsback is shown.
impact: The first screen looks broken on budget phones, and today's saved-advert 'Open it' and 'Pass Quick on' are unreachable there.

title: 'Find a trip' never shows trips that were listed through Quick, because it throws away every advert filed under 'Adventures'.
fix: In typeFilter, lowercase the category and also accept generic trip categories (e.g. `/^adventures?$/`) in addition to the want regex.
impact: Searchers are told a trip is not listed when it is, and Quick's trip listers get no Quick finds.

title: About 1 in 64 'Pass Quick on' invites fails for the person receiving it: she is told 'That invite is no longer open' and the sender waits for an Accept that never comes.
fix: Use `/[?&]i=([A-Za-z0-9_-]{8,40})(?=&|#|$)/` or `new URLSearchParams(location.search).get('i')` checked against the same character class.
impact: The hand-to-hand invite fails in front of both people for some pairs, with a misleading message.

title: 'Ask your traders instead' says her question went out to people as separate buzzes, but nothing is sent: the contacts are made-up examples.
fix: Until wired to a real send, label it 'Preview only' and disable Ask, or hide #lkask outside a local/dev origin.
impact: A real searcher waits for replies that will never come.

title: The 'fastest thing on this whole app' (an employer's reference) is only a pretend walk-through: an employer who types an email and a reference into it is told it worked, but nothing is saved or sent.
fix: Mark each vouch screen 'Preview — nothing is sent', make inputs read-only, and either wire a real reference-request action or remove the card until one exists.
impact: A lister who hands her phone to her employer loses a real reference and believes her trust score opened.

title: Every visit to Quick starts downloading 29 pictures the person may never see (23 trip destinations and 6 street scenes) plus duplicate server calls, slowing the first screen on 3G.
fix: Preload a category's pictures only when that flow starts; share one /quick/me promise between handlers; fetch /trust/catalogue lazily in drawDraft.
impact: The door and first taps are slower on weak data, and prepaid data is spent on pictures for categories she never opens.

title: Picking or typing any area other than six Pretoria/Johannesburg names makes Quick download every suburb in South Africa, in about 55 separate requests, just to guess the city.
fix: Skip the lookup when the area is already in QP.cities[QCITY]; resolve typed areas with a single `/geo/suburbs?name=&country=` call.
impact: On weak 3G this background download competes with the next screens and the save request.

title: The city she chose can be silently replaced: an area name that exists in two cities (e.g. Rosebank) is filed under whichever city comes first alphabetically, and a slow account lookup can switch her city mid-advert.
fix: Set `userCity=true` inside drawCityPick's onclick; keep window.QCITY when the picked area belongs to it; ignore the /quick/me city once a mode/city is already set.
impact: Her advert can be listed in a city she does not work in and get no introductions.

title: 'Which city?' offers only 14 South African cities and no 'my city is not here' option, so someone in Rustenburg, Welkom or Stellenbosch (or in Zimbabwe or Lesotho) must pick a city she does not live in.
fix: Add a dashed 'My city is not listed' chip that opens a free-text input, resolves it via `/geo/cities?q=`, and sets window.QCITY=null so the plain free 'where' card is used instead.
impact: Adverts get filed in the wrong city unless a typed area happens to be matched later, and people outside the list feel shut out.

title: Typing a price with a thousands comma, like '1,500', is read as R1.50: the rate screen says 'That is below the national minimum wage' and will not let her continue.
fix: Strip thousands separators first (e.g. `v.replace(/[\s,.](?=\d{3}(?:\D|$))/g,'')`) before converting a remaining ',' to '.'.
impact: Tradespeople and tutors typing normal amounts are blocked with a wrong, alarming message.

title: A person using TrustSquare in isiZulu (or another language) who taps 'In a hurry? 5-tap Quick advert' gets Quick in English.
fix: Fall back to `localStorage.getItem('ts_lang')` in the QLANG init (mapping 'st'→'nso', validated against QLANGS), or append `&lang=`+the app's language to both app-side Quick links.
impact: The language she already chose is lost at the hand-over into Quick.

title: Pressing Back (the ← button or the phone's Back) on 'See what they get' or 'Ask your traders' does not return to her advert or results; it deletes her last answer and reopens the previous question.
fix: Track a sub-screen flag (e.g. `atSub='vouch'|'traders'`) set in drawVouch/drawTraders and cleared in drawDraft/drawLookup; branch on it first in back.onclick.
impact: She loses answers and has to redo steps to get back to her advert or results.

title: After saving with an email, the confirmation never shows which address was used, so a typo goes unnoticed, and on the next advert the 'change' link does nothing.
fix: Show 'We emailed <address> — not right?' with a control that clears QUICK.member/HANDOVER.email and reopens the email box; make 'change' do the same.
impact: A mistyped address loses the way-back email and strands the advert, with no chance to correct it in Quick.

title: Her answers are kept only while the page stays open: if the save fails for lack of data and she leaves to fix it, or a cheap phone reloads the tab, the whole advert is gone.
fix: On every pick and on a failed save, persist a `ts_q_wip` snapshot to sessionStorage; on load, if recent, offer to restore it; clear it after a successful save.
impact: On weak networks and low-memory phones people have to rebuild the advert from the door.

title: For people who saved with the WhatsApp key or a phone code, the 'Open it ›' link on Quick's saved-advert card sends them to an email sign-in they cannot complete.
fix: Store `url: r.key_url||r.open_url||''` in ts_q_saved and use it as the card's href when present.
impact: The door's way back to her advert is a dead end for the Services default identity when she is not already signed in on that browser.

title: The 'saved' screen repeats itself ('Your advert is saved. Your advert is saved.', 'We emailed you a link' twice) and shows raw double hyphens ('--').
fix: When r.detail is present drop the generic line and the duplicate ar-small sentence; use '—' instead of '--' in these strings.
impact: Looks unpolished at the moment of success.

title: The 'Another option' typing card always talks as if she is writing her advert and always says 'the six above', even when she is searching or the list has 4, 9 or 11 choices.
fix: Make the copy mode-aware (find: 'Say what you are looking for.') and drop the count ('The ones above are only the ones we see most').
impact: Confusing wording; a searcher may think her search words will be published.

title: Nine of today's new 'kind' pictures (plumber, painter, pool care, cleaning, laundry and others) can never appear, because the Services screens never show the tiles they were attached to.
fix: Remove the services/homehelp entries from KIND-FIT-1, or retarget them at `PH['role_<key>']` for the matching SVC_ROLES keys.
impact: No visible harm, but the claimed fix for Services and Home help did not ship.

title: The 'Make your own advert — free' link under Services adverts opens Quick without the '‹ TrustSquare' way back.
fix: Add `from=app` to the href: `/quick/?from=app&src=listing-make`.
impact: Someone using the installed app has no visible way back to the advert she was reading.

title: 'Find a piece' (Collectors) never asks where she is, so unless the phone's city is known it only searches Pretoria and may say nothing is listed.
fix: Add a 'where' step to collectors.find, or query collectors without a city filter.
impact: A Durban or Cape Town collector can be told 'Nobody has listed this in Pretoria yet'.

title: The advert Quick writes can contain bare one-word sentences such as 'Certificate.' or 'Collect.', and an 'I speak English.' line she never saw before saving.
fix: Phrase per key (qual: 'Holds a trade certificate.', ship: 'Collect from me.'), and redraw the card text after svcFinish so the preview equals the saved description.
impact: Buyers read awkward adverts, and the saved text differs from what she approved.

title: In 'Find a pro' results, adverts without photos show an unrelated stock picture (a home cleaner on an electrician's advert, a technician on a nanny's), not marked as an example.
fix: Fall back to the searched role's own picture (`'role_'+svcPickIn(picks,'what').r`) or a neutral icon, and label it as an example photo.
impact: Misleading pictures on real people's adverts.

title: A worker who comes back after saving with her WhatsApp key sees 'Publishing as w-3f9a1c7b2e', a machine code instead of her name.
fix: In /quick/me return name null for key identities, or in Quick: if(d.key_identity && /^w-[0-9a-f]+$/.test(QUICK.name)) QUICK.name='You'.
impact: Confusing, and looks broken to a returning worker.

title: The picture tiles, day boxes, contact rows and the top-bar ← and ↻ are plain boxes rather than buttons, so screen-reader and keyboard users cannot tell they can be tapped or reach them.
fix: Render these as `<button type="button">` (or add role="button" tabindex="0" plus Enter/Space handling) and give #back/#home aria-labels.
impact: People using TalkBack or VoiceOver cannot complete an advert.

title: After any update goes live, a green 'new version' bar covers the whole bottom menu with only a Refresh button, and tapping it throws away an advert the seller is halfway through.
fix: Add a 'Later' (x) button; don't show the bar while any .modal-bg.open or #screen-sell-flow / #screen-edit-listing is active (queue it for the next goTo('home')); check on launch only, not on every visibilitychange.
impact: A seller who comes back from the camera mid-advert is pushed to 'Refresh' and silently loses every photo and answer; everyone else loses the bottom menu until they reload.

title: The floating 'English' language button sits on top of the main button of every advert (it reads '...est Introduction') and on the request, payment and Sell sheets.
fix: Lower its z-index below sheet/CTA layers and hide it behind an open sheet/detail/sell screen (e.g. via a body:has() rule), or keep only the header language pill on those screens.
impact: The core buyer button looks broken on every advert, and taps on its left fifth open the language menu instead of requesting the introduction or confirming a purchase.

title: Longer pop-up messages run off both sides of a phone screen, so error, safety and install instructions can't be read.
fix: Add `white-space:normal;width:max-content;max-width:calc(100vw - 32px);text-align:center;` to `.toast`.
impact: People can't read why an introduction was held, why publishing failed, or how to add the app on an iPhone - and the iPhone tip is never shown again.

title: If one background check fails on a weak connection, the whole app is replaced by a 'Marketplace Preview - Pre-launch access only' sign-in wall.
fix: Retry once (~2s) on fetch failure before falling back, and only showGate() on an explicit {valid:false} response.
impact: An ordinary visitor on a flaky connection is told the marketplace is closed to them and has to reload (close and reopen the installed app) to get back in.

title: The 'Top Up Tuppence' button shown when a seller's free AI Coach session is used up does nothing.
fix: Change both onclick handlers to `onclick="aaBuyPackFromWallet()"`.
impact: A seller ready to pay to keep using the AI Coach taps the button and nothing happens.

title: Every visit waits for the map library to download from a third-party site before anything appears, although the map is only used when someone switches Browse to map view.
fix: Remove the four unpkg tags from `<head>`; load Leaflet + MarkerCluster on demand inside setViewMode('map')/renderMap() reusing the aiLeaflet pattern.
impact: Slower first screen for everyone on SA mobile networks, and a white screen whenever unpkg is slow or down.

title: The footer links (Terms of Use, Privacy Policy, Contact) and the company registration line are white on a light grey page and practically invisible.
fix: Use the light-theme tokens instead: footer `color:var(--text-3)`, links `color:var(--text-2)`, `border-top:1px solid var(--border)`.
impact: Nobody can see the Terms, Privacy or Contact links or the company registration number at the bottom of the page.

title: Screen-reader users hear just 'button' for the save-heart on every advert, the back and save buttons on an advert page, and about 30 other icon-only buttons.
fix: Add aria-labels: wish-btn="Save advert" with aria-pressed, back/save controls their action names, close crosses "Close".
impact: Blind and low-vision users can't tell what these buttons do, including going back and saving adverts.

title: Adverts, category tiles, filter chips, the location picker and the language button are plain boxes rather than buttons, so keyboard users can't open them and screen readers don't announce them as buttons.
fix: Render as `<button>`/`<a href>`, or add role="button" tabindex="0" plus a delegated Enter/Space keydown handler.
impact: A keyboard-only user (e.g. on desktop) cannot open a single advert or change category; screen-reader users get no 'button' cue.

title: The 'In a hurry? 5-tap Quick advert' line in the Sell sheet is a thin 20-pixel strip right under 'Use a different account', easy to miss or to hit by accident.
fix: Add `padding:12px 0; margin-top:4px` to `.sell-quick-line`/`.sf-quick-line` for a ~44px tap target.
impact: Sellers who want the fast path can overlook it, and a thumb aimed at 'Use a different account' can land on the Quick door instead (or the reverse).

title: '5-tap Quick advert' and Quick's 'A few taps, no typing' promise don't match the service path, which asks five questions and makes her type her rate.
fix: Say 'In a hurry? Quick advert in about a minute' in both places and 'A few taps. Your advert, your language.' on the door (or give the rate step preset chips so no typing is needed).
impact: A hurried seller is promised five taps and no typing, then meets about ten taps and a keyboard - an avoidable dent in trust right at the hand-off.

title: Arriving in Quick from TrustSquare, the new '< TrustSquare' button is drawn on top of the TrustSquare logo, so the header shows two overlapping wordmarks.
fix: Hide the logo while the back-chip is shown (e.g. a `.has-tsback .logo{visibility:hidden}` class toggle), or render the chip inside the empty #back slot.
impact: The first screen after the hand-off looks broken.

title: On short phone screens the 'Request Introduction' sheet is taller than the screen, and its top (handle, title, advert name) is cut off with no way to scroll to it.
fix: Add `.modal{max-height:calc(100dvh - 12px);overflow-y:auto;}`.
impact: Buyers on small or older phones lose the sheet's heading and the name of the advert they are requesting.

title: Every visitor downloads about 200 KB of code and screens they won't use: the Adventures trip-guide data and three retired selling screens.
fix: Inject trip_essentials.js on first tripEssentialsPanel() use (or at least add defer); move retired screens to a fragment fetched on demand, or delete them.
impact: A slower start and more data on every visit over weak networks.

title: Each time someone returns to the app it re-downloads the whole start page just to compare a version number.
fix: Serve a tiny /version.json (or compare an ETag via HEAD) and check at most every 10-15 minutes.
impact: Extra mobile data (about 54 KB per app switch, plus a duplicate download at every launch) for prepaid users.

title: Tapping a match notification no longer opens the Quick door (fix confirmed), but it can still bring forward a Terms or Support tab, and it never opens the match itself.
fix: Prefer a client whose pathname is '/', focus and `navigate('/?wl_match='+id)` (or postMessage + goTo('home')); otherwise `openWindow('/?wl_match='+id)`.
impact: A buyer who taps 'New match in your wishlist' can land on the Terms page, or on whatever app screen they last left, instead of on the match.

title: The service worker makes every page open wait for it to start up, yet it adds nothing because it caches nothing and only passes pages through.
fix: Enable `self.registration.navigationPreload` in `activate` and await `event.preloadResponse` before `fetch(req)` in the handler — this keeps the A2HS-enabling real fetch handler and the offline page intact while removing the startup-serialization delay.
impact: Every launch and every hand-off (including Quick -> TrustSquare) starts a little later on slow phones.

title: Form labels such as 'Your name *' aren't connected to their boxes, so screen readers read the grey example text instead (the suburb box is read as 'Brooklyn').
fix: Add `for=` to each label (or wrap the input inside it).
impact: Screen-reader users hear example values instead of field names and aren't told which fields are required.

title: The small lines saying what an AI tool charged and how much Tuppence is left are light grey on white and hard to read.
fix: Use `var(--text-3)` (or another ≥4.5:1 token) for these lines, at ≥11px.
impact: Money information is the hardest text on the card to read, especially outdoors on a phone.

title: Several often-used buttons are smaller than a fingertip: the save-heart on each advert (28 px), the header 'Sign in' (28 px tall), the grid/map switch (32x28) and the For You settings cog (16x20).
fix: Increase hit areas to ≥40px via padding or a transparent ::after overlay while keeping the visual icon size.
impact: Mis-taps: aiming for the heart often opens the advert instead of saving it, and the small header and toggle buttons need repeated tries.

title: Quick stops people from pinch-zooming the page on Android phones.
fix: Drop `maximum-scale=1` from Quick's viewport meta (keep viewport-fit=cover).
impact: Low-vision users can't enlarge Quick's text or pictures.

title: Neither app turns motion off for people who ask their phone to reduce motion; Quick's door keeps pulsing and cross-fading photos every 4 seconds.
fix: Add a global `@media (prefers-reduced-motion:reduce)` rule to ms.css and quick.html disabling animation/transition, and skip `setInterval(cycleHero,...)` when the media query matches.
impact: Motion-sensitive users get endless pulsing and sliding they cannot stop.

title: Quick's back, restart, category arrows, language chips and answer tiles are plain boxes rather than buttons, so keyboards can't reach them and screen readers only hear symbols such as the arrow and circle glyphs.
fix: Render these as `<button type="button">` with aria-labels ('Back', 'Start again', 'Previous/Next category').
impact: Screen-reader and switch users struggle to go back, restart or pick an answer.

title: If a Featured card's category picture fails to load, a broken-image icon stays instead of the intended category emoji.
fix: Escape the nested quote as `\\'` so the emitted attribute carries a literal backslash-quote, or replace the inline handler with a named helper: `onerror="catImgFallback(this,'${_fCfg.icon}')"`.
impact: Occasional broken-image boxes on the Home 'Featured' strip.

title: A seller can hide web-page code in an advert's 'service type', 'subject', 'level', 'mode' or 'availability' and it runs in the browser of every buyer who opens the advert; a quote mark in the title or photo list does the same on the Browse grid, without anyone opening the advert.
fix: Escape every seller value at render with one helper (e.g. _wlEsc, which also escapes quotes): cardHtml img src/alt and text, openDetail chips 5228-5236 and dmeta area 5180, advNearbyStrip 3161, openBEASellerProfile 4781, msRenderHistory/msRenderWishlist. Server: add subject, level, mode, service_type, service_class, availability (and other free-text columns) to `_TEXT_KEYS`, make `_pt` encode `"`, and run each `[photos:]` entry through `_URL_OK` on write.
impact: Any visitor can have her signed-in session used (introductions, profile, adverts) or her details sent away just by browsing or opening one planted advert.

title: A seller who pays for Starter or Pro from the Plans screen is charged but her plan is never switched on — she comes back to the home page, still on Free, with no message.
fix: Use the working return address in both places: `window.location.origin + '/?ps_sub_return=1'` (as ms.js 6836 does); in the ps_sub_return handler show a success toast and open the hub when there is no sob_resume; and have the webhook apply `seller_subscription` charges as a server-side backstop.
impact: R90 or R360 is taken, the seller stays blocked at 2 adverts and gets no monthly Tuppence grant.

title: A Local Market advert opened from a link (Quick's Find, a WhatsApp Status share, Quick's 'See my advert') opens on the ordinary advert page, which asks the buyer for 1 Tuppence and charges it when the seller accepts — Local Market is supposed to be free for buyers.
fix: In openDetail (and the DEEPLINK fetch branch) send Local Market adverts to their own page: `if(l.cat==='LocalMarket'){ lmOpenDetail(String(l.id).replace(/^bea_/,'')); return; }`; server-side, refuse POST /intros for local_market listings (point to /local-market/intro).
impact: A buyer with no Tuppence is told she must buy some to contact a market seller; one with Tuppence pays 1T for a free introduction, and the seller-pays charge and her no-show protection are skipped.

title: Every 30 seconds the app throws away its list of adverts while it downloads a fresh one; if she taps 'Request Introduction' in that moment — or at any time on an advert from another city, such as one opened from Quick's Find — nothing happens, or the form closes and her message is lost.
fix: Download first, then swap: build the new city list and replace only the rows it returns (keep adverts that were fetched individually, e.g. mark them `_pinned`), never empty LISTINGS before the await; in _openModalNow/submitIntro, if findListing fails, re-fetch /listings/<id> instead of crashing, and clear the form only after the request succeeds.
impact: The main buying action silently fails, most often for buyers arriving from Quick in other cities, sometimes after she has typed her message.

title: If her sign-in has ended on the server (for example she signed out on another device) but the phone still remembers her email, a link from Quick opens an empty hub that greets her as a first-timer — her draft isn't shown and nothing tells her to sign in again.
fix: On a draft landing (and once at start-up), check the session with a 'user' GET (e.g. /users/<email>/subscription or /quick/me); on 401 clear ms_aa_email, prefill si-email from ts_quick_email, keep ts_land_draft and goTo('signin'). When msLandDraft gives up, say so: 'This advert is waiting on another email — sign in with the one you used in Quick'.
impact: She believes her advert is gone and is steered to make it again (a duplicate that uses a slot) instead of signing in.

title: Arriving from Quick while signed out, she is told her advert 'opens straight after' she signs in — but after the 6-digit code (or Google/Apple) the app reloads to the home page instead of her advert.
fix: At the end of _msInit: `if(sessionStorage.getItem('ts_land_draft') && _msIsSignedIn()){ goTo('dashboard'); msLandDraft(); }` — this covers the code reload and the OAuth return in one place.
impact: The most likely drop-off point of the hand-off: she lands on the marketplace front page and must discover My Hub herself to publish.

title: Choosing another city from the city badge doesn't load that city's adverts: Browse keeps showing the old city's adverts under the new city's name and the category tiles drop to '0 listings' for up to 30 seconds — and the choice is forgotten on the next visit.
fix: In selectCity: remove live adverts, call loadLiveListings(0) and localStorage.setItem('ms_user_city', name); add a request counter in loadLiveListings so a late answer for the previous city is ignored.
impact: Every buyer outside Pretoria sees wrong adverts or 'nothing here' right after choosing her city — the first thing she does, on every visit.

title: The phone's Back button never goes back one screen inside TrustSquare: from an advert, the hub, an edit form or the sell flow it leaves the app altogether (back to Quick, WhatsApp, or it closes the installed app) and anything typed is lost.
fix: In goTo(name) call history.pushState({s:name}, '') for user-initiated moves (not during start-up) and add window.onpopstate = e => goTo((e.state&&e.state.s)||'home') without pushing; after a draft/listing landing push the landed screen on top of a 'home' entry so the first Back stays inside the app.
impact: On Android, Back is the normal way to move around; here it silently exits and discards her work mid-form.

title: After she taps the heart (Save) on an advert's page, that page's back arrow stops working; the same happens after she opens a 'Stay nearby' advert from an advert page.
fix: Set window._msRerenderFlag=true in toggleWishDetail (and in the advNearbyStrip chip's onclick) before calling openDetail; better, toggle the heart icon's fill/stroke in place without a full re-render.
impact: She is stuck on the advert unless she finds the bottom menu (the phone Back leaves the app, see the Back finding).

title: Saved adverts are not kept: the heart says 'Added to saved', but the list is empty the next time she opens the app, and My Space always says 'No saved listings'.
fix: Persist wishlist to localStorage('ms_saved', JSON.stringify([...wishlist])) on every toggle, restore it into the wishlist Set at startup, and have renderSaved fetch ids missing from LISTINGS via GET /listings/<id>.
impact: Buyers lose the adverts they saved to decide on later, and the two 'saved' views contradict each other.

title: After tapping an advert in Quick's Find, the advert's back arrow goes to TrustSquare's Browse for Pretoria — not back to her Quick results — and nothing on screen leads back to Quick.
fix: When magicLink.src==='quick-find', label the detail back arrow 'Back to Quick' and use history.back(); have Quick append &city=<her city> to the deep link and read it into activeCity on load.
impact: A Sandton or Bellville visitor who uses the on-screen arrow lands in an unrelated Pretoria list and loses her way back to Quick.

title: The 'Do work like this yourself? Make your own advert — free' link under Services adverts is still a one-way door: Quick shows no way back to TrustSquare, and the tap is counted as coming from a WhatsApp Status.
fix: Change the link to /quick/?from=app&src=detail-make so Quick shows the way back and the funnel can tell this tap apart from a real WhatsApp Status share.
impact: A buyer who tries Quick from an advert cannot get back to the advert she was reading, and the funnel cannot tell in-app taps from Status traffic.

title: An advert opened from a link (Quick's Find, a Status share, an email card) only starts downloading after two location look-ups and the whole city advert list have finished, so on 3G she watches the home page and then a Browse flash first.
fix: In the ?listing= branch call openDetail('bea_'+id) immediately (DEEPLINK-FETCH-1 already fetches /listings/<id> when not found locally) and start loadLiveListings() in parallel with _resolveActiveCity() rather than chained after it.
impact: Several extra seconds on the key hand-off tap, on top of the known L16 page weight.

title: Search results can belong to an older search: on a slow connection an earlier search that finishes late overwrites the newer one (or re-filters the grid after she cleared the box), and nothing shows that a search is running.
fix: Add a monotonic `const seq=++_msSearchSeq` at the top of msRunSearch and `if(seq!==_msSearchSeq) return;` after every await; show a 'Searching…' state in #results-count while a search is in flight.
impact: She sees results or 'no matches' that don't fit what is in the box, or a filtered grid after clearing her search.

title: While the app is open it re-downloads every advert in the city (up to 200, with full descriptions) every 30 seconds and rebuilds the grid, featured strip and counts — even while she reads one advert or has switched to another app.
fix: Skip the tick when document.hidden is true or the active screen is not home/browse, stretch the interval to several minutes, and add a since=/ETag so an unchanged list is cheap.
impact: Steady drain of prepaid data and battery, and periodic jank on low-end phones.

title: Each time she switches back to the app it downloads the whole app page again to look for updates, and after any release two 'new version' bars appear that cannot be closed — one covers the bottom menu, the other sits over the middle of the 'Request Introduction' button and reloads the page if tapped.
fix: Consolidate to one checker, throttle it to roughly every 10 minutes, fetch a tiny version marker instead of the whole page, and give the bar a close (x) placed above .bnav/.sticky-cta rather than over them.
impact: Extra data on every WhatsApp <-> TrustSquare switch, and after each deploy (several a day) the bottom menu is hidden and a mis-tap on the main button reloads the app, losing anything typed.

title: After one failed background refresh the Local Market tile says 'Connecting…' for the rest of the visit, and after four failures in a row it becomes a 'Tap to refresh' button that no longer opens Local Market until the app is reloaded.
fix: On a successful loadLiveListings, reset #lm-home-count text (or call initLMHomeTile()) and restore lmTile.onclick=()=>goTo('local-market'); offer the retry as a separate small link instead of replacing the tile's main action.
impact: On patchy mobile data or during a server restart, Local Market becomes unreachable from the home screen.

title: After she signs in through a link (Quick's key link or an emailed sign-in link) the hub and wallet show 0 Tuppence until the app is reloaded.
fix: Extract the balance fetch into a msSyncBalance() helper and call it again immediately after a successful ?signin= verify (and after Quick's key-link sign-in), not just once early in _msInit.
impact: A seller with a balance sees 0T and may top up again for nothing.
